purpose: Choose the biggest indexing path from flame + timers after the JRuby call-host probe showed that door is cheap.

profiles.serial_note: RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 and one CPU lane. Wall ~19s. Samply self-time is dominated by Tokio idle (~66% unsafe_cell), so serial whole-process flames are not a clean CPU map.

flame_limitations: Parallel Rayon stacks often lose FactCollector frames; Prism ModuleNode::body / prism.c appear as ~60–97% inclusive without naming the Rust owner.
Serial whole-process samply mixes reactor wait with CPU work.
JrubyImportProvider name on earlier flames was frequent but stopwatch-proved ~0.23s of handler CPU vs ~5.9s project wall.

trusted_combined_ranking.path: project file fact collection (Prism parse + AST walk / FactCollector dual pass)
trusted_combined_ranking.why: Warm one-server phase timer: project ~5.3–5.9s of ~10.7–11s ready. Flame consistently shows Prism visitation as the deep CPU leaf during that phase. Prior accepted symbolized profile (v195) attributed file fact collection ~39.3% inclusive and call handling ~15.1%.
trusted_combined_ranking.not: JRuby call-host handlers (~0.23s measured), resolve-cache, gem prefetch overlap

trusted_combined_ranking.path: dependency gem bind / postcard deserialize (warm) or produce (cold)
trusted_combined_ranking.why: Dependencies phase ~3.7s warm; postcard appears in flames; cold gem rebuild can dominate wall.
Runtime phase ~2.5s; classpath/java product timers material.

chosen_next_path: rank 1 — project file fact collection / Prism AST walk under FileProcessor (including the measured double walk: collect_direct_facts then FactCollector::visit)
next_measurement_shape: Prefer a synchronous FileProcessor-only microbench/profile over whole-process samply so Rayon/Tokio cannot hide the owner; or add phase timers around parse vs seed walk vs full visit vs replace_facts per file batch.
